indicators.note: a medicine swallowed the letter I, so I goes inside the medicine word

parts.note: senna is a laxative medicine made from a plant's pods

explanation.surface: A patient complains about a brown medicine they have just gulped down.
explanation.definitionFit: Sienna is an earthy pigment, a shade of reddish or yellowish brown.

clue.text: Mediator flabbergasted with me: that's excessive!

indicators.note: someone flabbergasted is thrown into confusion, so these letters get jumbled

explanation.surface: A mediator, astonished at the speaker, exclaims that something has gone too far.
explanation.definitionFit: Immoderate means going beyond reasonable limits, a synonym of excessive.

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the synonym for worthless is cut off

parts.note: something worthless is 'no use'

explanation.surface: A grumble about an unending supply of useless ability.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' drops the last E from NO USE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nous is British slang for common sense or practical cleverness, a kind of aptitude.

indicators.note: one placed in the princess's name means the letter goes inside it

parts.note: Princess Alexandra is a member of the British royal family
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A princess is spotted in harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexandria is the great Egyptian harbour city on the Mediterranean.

definitions.meaning: to people a place is to live in it, a verb

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether certain people wore monastic robes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'People' is a verb here, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To people a town is to occupy or live in it; split in two, the word describes wearing a monk's robe.

definitions.meaning: to pull sharply is to jerk or tug
an American, 'the pond' being the Atlantic seen from Britain

explanation.surface: An instruction to haul a person over a stretch of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A yank is a sudden tug; a Yank is informal for a person from the USA.

clue.text: Greek character, after the due time, left individual collector initially concerned with this hobby

parts.note: phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
arriving after the due time is being late
I as a single individual, the first-person pronoun

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of collector is used

explanation.surface: A rambling description of a Greek fellow turning up late to meet a collector.
explanation.walkthrough: The hobby is the collector's, so the definition sits at the end: 'concerned with this hobby' means relating to stamp collecting.
explanation.definitionFit: Philatelic means relating to philately, the collecting of postage stamps.

parts.note: roses grow in a flower bed, so a pest there could be called a bug of the bed

explanation.surface: Someone wonders if a parasite has turned up at Rose's home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like a woman's name; read it as the flower, whose place is a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedbug is a small insect that feeds on human blood, usually in mattresses.

clue.text: Charlie's excited consuming a new cheese

indicators.note: the excited letters consume, that is take inside, the following pieces
excited letters are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: Charlie gets thrilled while eating a fresh cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges CHARLIES (the apostrophe ignored) into LCASHIRE, and 'consuming' puts A and N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancashire is a crumbly English cheese named after the county in north-west England.

clue.text: Joseph with some cans of beer for average man in USA

parts.note: Joe is a short form of Joseph
a six-pack is a pack of six beer cans

explanation.surface: Joseph turns up with beer as a gift for an ordinary American guy.
explanation.definitionFit: Joe Sixpack is American slang for the typical working-class man in the street.

indicators.note: inside means the letters are found within the word clambered

explanation.surface: A ship's captain scrambled aboard into the vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skipper' suggests a captain; here it is one who skips, a frisky young sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: A young sheep gambols and leaps about, so it is playfully a jumper.

parts.note: a leg supports a table or chair
the letter O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A description of a ring-shaped toy that holds something up.
explanation.definitionFit: Lego is a brand of plastic interlocking building bricks for children.

explanation.surface: Someone is reluctant to tell the truth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not inclined' looks like reluctance; it means horizontal.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on a flat plane means level ground, and the idiom also means being genuine and straightforward.

clue.text: Habit that's extremely tense and exciting

definitions.meaning: a nervous habit of chewing one's fingertips
describes a thriller or close contest full of suspense

explanation.surface: A description of a gripping, nerve-wracking habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnawing the fingernails is a nervous habit; a suspenseful finish is described by the same compound.

clue.text: Cooking thus, US barman used an acid salt

parts.note: baking is a way of cooking in an oven
so means thus, in that way
a DA, district attorney, is an American lawyer, someone called to the bar

explanation.surface: An American bartender cooks with an acidic salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barman' looks like a pub worker; it means a member of the bar, a lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodium bicarbonate is an acid salt, the raising agent used in cakes.

parts.note: the people in their care are young children, not low fees

explanation.surface: Someone notes that certain service providers keep their fees modest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charges' reads as fees; it means those in one's care.
explanation.definitionFit: Nannies look after young children, who are literally small.

indicators.note: in front says the agent goes before the unknown

parts.note: a factor is an agent who does business for another
y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Instructions to place a mysterious spy at the forefront.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a planted spy, matching 'agent'; it is an industrial plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A manufacturing plant is a works where goods are produced.

definitions.meaning: a songbird that sings while rising high in the air
a prank or bit of horseplay

explanation.surface: A successful person's clever ploy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-flier' suggests an ambitious person; it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The songbird climbs high as it sings, and as a noun the word also means a frolic or prank.

clue.text: Tense during peculiar ritual in name only

indicators.note: a letter during the anagram sits within it
peculiar means odd, so the word ritual is rearranged

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A strange ceremony performed under nervous strain, purely for show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peculiar' turns RITUAL into TIULAR, and 'during' puts T inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A titular head holds the title but none of the real authority.

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a priest's title
elation is great happiness

explanation.surface: A volume brings a clergyman delight.
explanation.definitionFit: The final book of the New Testament is known as the Apocalypse or the Book of Revelation.

parts.note: drawing straight lines on paper, and also an official judgement

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a clear-cut verdict is being reached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'straight' seems to mean frank; it also refers to drawing lines with a ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge's verdict is a pronouncement on a point; lining paper with a ruler gives the same word.

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
to hew is to cut with an axe

explanation.surface: Instructions to eat a chilled slice of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Chewing is grinding food with the teeth, a basic part of eating.

clue.text: Be idle with the French gazetteer included

indicators.note: included means the gazetteer piece is placed within the French article

parts.note: le is the French for 'the'
an A to Z is a street atlas or gazetteer of a city

explanation.surface: Someone lounges around with a French place guide.
explanation.walkthrough: An A–Z is a British book of street maps.
explanation.definitionFit: To laze is to lounge about doing nothing.

indicators.note: upset means overturned and disordered, so request's letters are jumbled

parts.note: Ian is a typically Scottish first name

explanation.surface: A horseman's request has annoyed a man from Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: An equestrian is a person who rides horses.

definitions.meaning: the outer border or rim of something, what lies on the outside

explanation.surface: The benefit that an underdog enjoys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outsider' suggests an underdog; it is the outer side, the border.
explanation.definitionFit: The rim of a thing is its outermost part, and having the upper hand over a rival is the same word.

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to moor a boat is to tie it up

explanation.surface: A spot for fastening a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Room means available area, as in leg-room.

clue.text: States part that's a young country

parts.note: something young is new
England is a country of the UK

explanation.surface: A region described as a youthful nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'young country' looks like the definition; the definition is 'States part'.
explanation.definitionFit: The north-eastern region of six US states is called New England.

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
most means the greater part

explanation.surface: A vote nearing a majority of fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: Approaching, as an adverb meaning nearly, is a synonym of not quite.
